report.summary: Chunk 2 of 6: defines projection_to_graph, declared_partition, helper functions, and fiedler_report with claims about algebraic connectivity interpretation.
risks: fiedler_report | medium | Returns _unavailable when eigensolver fails; the error message is passed through, which may leak internal info. | Check if error messages are sanitized or logged.
fiedler_report | low | Uses 'method="lanczos"' which may not converge; fallback to another method is not implemented. | Consider adding fallback method.

projection_to_graph | low | 'modules' is obtained via getattr(report, 'modules', ()) which may be empty; behavior is undefined if report has no 'modules'. | Verify that report always has 'modules' attribute.

handoff.purpose: Defines projection_to_graph, declared_partition, helper functions (_communities, _giant), and fiedler_report.

symbols.name: projection_to_graph
symbols.note: Undirected projection of a ReachReport; filters by scope_prefixes, trims edges to known nodes, returns graph from graph_from_edges.

symbols.name: declared_partition
symbols.note: Groups modules by declared_package, returns dict of package to sorted module list.

symbols.name: _communities
symbols.note: Converts partition mapping to list of node sets covering graph nodes; handles missing nodes.

symbols.name: _giant
symbols.note: Returns the largest connected component subgraph; tie-breaker by first node name.

symbols.name: fiedler_report
symbols.note: Computes algebraic connectivity and Fiedler vector, returns dict with connectivity, boundary_agreement, etc. Handles disconnected graphs via giant component.

claims.text: Every node is a repo-relative .py path, exactly as docs/architecture-state.json names them, so a number reported here can be pasted next to an island or shim from the same snapshot.
claims.why: The chunk does not contain docs/architecture-state.json or any code that validates node names; cannot verify.

claims.text: scope_prefixes restricts the graph to modules under those path prefixes. Default None means MEASURE EVERYTHING -- no hidden filtering
claims.why: Code shows: if scope_prefixes: filter modules by startswith; else no filter.

claims.text: It exists because the whole-repo reading is dominated by a partition artifact: tests/ is ~half the modules, and test files import the code under test and never each other, so the test package scores leak_rate 1.0 with zero internal edges. That is CORRECT and MEANINGLESS
claims.why: No code in this chunk computes leak_rate or references test behavior; claim about test package behavior cannot be verified.

claims.text: reach may record an import of something outside the scanned tree; those are real facts but not nodes of this graph, and inventing nodes for them would inflate every denominator below.
claims.why: Code trims edges: trimmed = {src: [t for t in tgts if t in known] ...]}, so external targets are removed.

claims.text: This is the partition the metrics below judge. It is read off the tree, not proposed by any algorithm -- the whole point is to score a human decision.
claims.why: No code in this chunk shows how the partition is used by metrics; claim about scoring is not verifiable.

claims.text: Reported on the largest connected component when the graph is disconnected: a disconnected graph has algebraic connectivity exactly 0 and no unique Fiedler vector, and fabricating one would be the numerology this module exists to prevent. Both the global 0.0 and the component value are returned, labelled, so neither can be quoted as the other.
claims.why: Code checks connectedness, uses _giant for component; returns dict with 'algebraic_connectivity' (global) and 'component_algebraic_connectivity' (not shown but implied). However, the actual return dict is not fully shown; the claim about labelling is partially verifiable.

claims.text: WHAT TO DO WITH THE NUMBER ... agreement ~1.0 -- a REAL SEAM ... agreement ~0.5 -- a FALSE WALL ... algebraic_connectivity near 0 ... algebraic_connectivity high ...
claims.why: Interpretation guidance is not enforced by code; no validation of agreement values exists in this chunk.

observations.what: projection_to_graph uses getattr(report, 'modules', ()) which may return an empty tuple if 'modules' missing; behavior is silent.
fiedler_report catches Exception from eigensolver and returns _unavailable with the exception message; this may leak internal details.
observations.where: fiedler_report line: except Exception as exc

observations.what: The docstring for fiedler_report describes a return dict with keys like 'algebraic_connectivity' and 'boundary_agreement', but the actual return statement is not in this chunk; the claim about 'component_algebraic_connectivity' is not verified.
The function _giant uses tie-breaker sorted(c)[0] when components have equal size; this is arbitrary.
